The generated `candidate-manifest.json` binds every retained artifact and this
report to the exact source revision. Candidate creation does not publish, tag,
or mutate an external provider.

## Test and packaging evidence

This tracked report describes the required gates but does not claim that a
particular candidate passed them. Release-specific test counts, coverage,
artifact digests, and attestations belong to the immutable candidate workflow
and its generated manifest; they must never be copied forward by a version
bump.

The release workflow repeats the release-facing checks, builds the canonical
Web assets once at the candidate SHA, verifies wheel/sdist/npm parity, and emits
SBOM, license, provenance, manifest, and checksum evidence.

## Migration and recovery evidence

`giga state upgrade` performs a backup-first, journaled, idempotent transition
from 0.6 state into native agent profiles and Project Catalog records. It blocks
on conflicts and unsupported source versions, verifies every staged payload,
atomically promotes the target, and preserves the backup until verification is
complete. The focused tests cover dry-run, successful upgrade, repeat runs,
interruption before and after promotion, corrupt journals, target conflicts,
and restoration from backup.

The 0.8.1→0.9 transition is additive: existing sessions are not rewritten into
Thread Relay records, attachment charset evidence is optional for old records,
Effective Instructions is derived read-only state, and route overlays do not
become defaults. Rollback stops only owned sidecar leases and disables new route
admission while retaining source sessions and immutable launch/delivery
receipts. An older executable may ignore or quarantine unknown additive records;
it must not rewrite them or silently restore a legacy gateway route.

## Security review contract

The candidate review covers native executable launch, local ACP stdio, bounded
Thread Relay authority, gateway routes/overlays, attachment decoding, Effective
Instructions discovery, project and route selection, MCP Apps iframe/resource
boundaries, evidence and capsule signing, state migration, and the multi-registry
supply chain. Candidate gates must fail closed on executable identity, source
revision, actor/project/workspace binding, capability, authority, revision,
digest, signature, migration journal, or artifact parity drift. Review
completion and findings belong to the candidate evidence rather than this
reusable source document.

## Run capsule evidence

The candidate includes `run-capsule-fixture.json`, the content-free read-only
input fixture used by the release journey. Tests export it into a signed capsule,
verify the archive offline, reject tampering and unsafe archive paths, and retain
the explicit `correctness_claimed=false` boundary: a valid signature proves
integrity and provenance, not task correctness.

## External pins

`external-evidence.json` records the exact ACP Python SDK, Pi ACP profile, and
MCP Apps versions, evidence digests, registry integrity, and admitted transport
constraints used by this candidate.

## Known limitations

- Pi and other native agents must already be installed and authenticated by the
  operator; GigaLoom does not install them or take ownership of their accounts.
- ACP v1 is local stdio only. Remote ACP transport and automatic fallback are
  not admitted.
- MCP Apps v1 admits reviewed local, read-only integrations only and falls back
  to evidence-only rendering when the Web host cannot be trusted.
- Provider and registry live checks require external credentials and are not
  exercised by local non-live validation.
- Codex Responses and managed ACP routes through `gpt2giga 0.3.0` are technical
  previews; Claude is vendor-unsupported and requires acknowledgement; Gemini
  custom-endpoint launch remains blocked.
